sources.entry: Sunshine - Remote game stream host for Moonlight with support up to 120 frames per second and 4K resolution. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C++/deb/Docker

summary.one_liner: Sunshine is a self-hosted game stream host that lets Moonlight clients connect to and play games running on a host machine, with hardware or software video encoding and a web UI for configuration and pairing.
keywords: stream pc games to another device
game streaming alternative to nvidia gamestream
summary.what_it_does: Sunshine runs as the host side of a game streaming setup: Moonlight clients on other devices connect to it and receive the host's screen and send back input. It supports hardware encoding on AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPUs (via APIs such as AMF, NVENC, QuickSync, VAAPI, Video Toolbox, and Vulkan Video) as well as software encoding. The README lists screen capture methods per platform, including DXGI, KMS/DRM, NvFBC, ScreenCaptureKit, Wayland (wlroots), X11, and XDG Desktop Portal. It emulates several gamepad types on the host, with varying support per OS. A web UI handles configuration and client pairing from a browser, either on the local server or a mobile device. Full documentation is hosted on Read the Docs.
use_cases: stream games from a home PC to a laptop or phone
run a self-hosted cloud gaming server
pair Moonlight clients with a host PC
stream games at high frame rates and 4K resolution
use GPU hardware encoding for low-latency game streaming
emulate a controller for remote game play
notable: Hardware encoding across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPUs, plus software encoding fallback
Broad screen capture support including Wayland (wlroots), KMS/DRM, and Windows Graphics Capture
Gamepad emulation for Xbox, DualShock/DS4, DualSense, and Switch Pro profiles on the host
Browser-based web UI for configuration and client pairing
caveats: Gamepad emulation on some platforms requires a separately installed and licensed Virtual HID Broker, and some features are missing on certain OSes
Requires Wi-Fi or ethernet with 5GHz 802.11ac or better network for good results; 4K and HDR need more capable GPUs
README warns that the system requirement tables are a work in progress and should not be used for purchasing decisions
